source.title: Steinberg Groups for Jordan Pairs - An Introduction with Open Problems

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary Jordan pair V, describe the full normal subgroup structure of its projective elementary group PE(V); equivalently, classify all normal subgroups of PE(V).

evidence.quote: Given a Jordan pair V , describe all normal subgroups of PE(V ).

accepted.question_text: For more general Jordan pairs V than those covered by Loos's cited theorems, determine whether the same perfectness and simplicity criteria for the projective elementary group PE(V) hold: is PE(V) perfect if and only if V has no simple factors isomorphic to (F_2, F_2), (F_3, F_3), or (H_2(F_2), H_2(F_2)); and is PE(V) simple if and only if V is simple and is not isomorphic to any of those exceptional Jordan pairs?

evidence.quote: In view of the results of [Lo5] it is natural to ask: when is PE(V ) a perfect group, when is it simple?
Thus, the problem is to find out if these two theorems of [Lo5] hold for more general Jordan pairs.

accepted.question_text: Let I be an ideal of a Jordan pair V, let can: V -> V/I be the canonical quotient map, and let PE(can): PE(V) -> PE(V/I) be the induced surjective homomorphism on projective elementary groups. Define the relative projective elementary group PE(V, I) to be the kernel of PE(can). Describe PE(V, I) by explicit generators and defining relations.

evidence.quote: the canonical map can : V → V /I induces a surjective group homomorphism PE(can) : PE(V ) → PE(V /I).
Problem: describe PE(V, I) by generators and relations.

accepted.question_text: Let V be a Jordan pair defined over a field F with a fully idempotent root grading R by root spaces V_alpha, and assume this grading is a division grading: all root spaces V_alpha are Jordan division pairs, meaning that for every nonzero x in V_alpha^sigma, the endomorphism Q(x) restricted to V_alpha^{-sigma} is invertible. In the low-rank cases 2 <= rank R <= 4, if the Steinberg group St(V, R) is not centrally closed, must every root space V_alpha be one-dimensional over F and must the pair consisting of the 3-graded root system and the field size be one of the exceptional cases from table (3.2.1): A_1^2 over a field of size 2 or 4; A_1^3 or A_2^3 over a field of size 2; C_2^her over a field of size 2; B_3^qf over a field of size 3; C_3^her over a field of size 2; or D_4^alt over a field of size 2?

evidence.quote: the fully idempotent root grading R of V is a division grading in the sense that all root spaces Vα are Jordan division pairs
(C) If St(V, R) is not centrally closed then dimF Vα = 1 for all α ∈ R1 and F satisfies the restrictions of table (3.2.1).
(R, R1 )    A12    A13 or A23   Cher 2      Bqf 3    Cher 3      Dalt 4

accepted.question_text: In the rank-one case, let J be a division Jordan algebra and let St(J) be the associated rank-one Steinberg group considered for the Jordan pair (J, J). Is St(J) centrally closed for every such J except when J is the finite field F_q with q in {2, 3, 4, 9}?

evidence.quote: V is a division pair and is therefore isomorphic to the Jordan pair (J, J) of a division Jordan algebra J.
(Q) Is St(J) centrally closed whenever J 6= Fq with q ∈ {2, 3, 4, 9} ?

accepted.question_text: Let (R, R_1) be a 3-graded root system, let V be a Jordan pair with a root grading by R, and let pi: St(V, R) -> PE(V) be the canonical homomorphism from the Steinberg group of the root graded Jordan pair to the projective elementary group, determined on generators by sending x_sigma(u) to exp_sigma(u). Assuming R is irreducible and has finite rank, find sufficient conditions under which Ker(pi) is central in St(V, R).

evidence.quote: There exists a group homomorphism π : St(V, R) → PE(V ), uniquely determined by π xσ (u) = expσ (u),
The problem here is: find sufficient conditions for Ker(π) to be central if R has finite rank.

accepted.question_text: For split root graded Jordan pairs V, can van der Kallen's basis-free presentation method be generalized to treat the Steinberg group St(V, R) uniformly, in a way that avoids case-by-case distinctions among root-system types?

evidence.quote: The quoted papers all use the same method, pioneered by [vdK], namely a “basis-free presentation of St(V, R)”.
Can the method of [vdK] be generalized to treat St(V, R), V split root graded, in a case-free manner?
